events.title: Charles the Fat is deposed at an assembly in Frankfurt
events.description: The Frankish magnates deposed Emperor Charles the Fat, the last Carolingian to rule a united kingdom of the Franks, at an assembly in Frankfurt. His nephew Arnulf of Carinthia became king of East Francia, and the empire fragmented permanently.
events.html: The Frankish magnates deposed Emperor Charles the Fat, the last Carolingian to rule a united kingdom of the Franks, at an assembly in Frankfurt. His nephew Arnulf of Carinthia became king of East Francia, and the empire fragmented permanently.

events.title: John Balliol is chosen King of Scots over Robert de Brus
events.description: Noblemen headed by Edward I of England chose John Balliol as King of Scots over Robert de Brus, ending the succession dispute known as the Great Cause. Balliol was deposed after the English invasion of 1296.
events.html: Noblemen headed by Edward I of England chose John Balliol as King of Scots over Robert de Brus, ending the succession dispute known as the Great Cause. Balliol was deposed after the English invasion of 1296.

events.title: Elizabeth I becomes queen of England
events.description: On the death of her half-sister Mary I, the 25-year-old Elizabeth succeeded to the throne. Her 44-year reign brought a Protestant church settlement, the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a flowering of literature.
events.html: On the death of her half-sister Mary I, the 25-year-old Elizabeth succeeded to the throne. Her 44-year reign brought a Protestant church settlement, the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a flowering of literature.

events.title: Sigismund III Vasa succeeds his father John III as king of Sweden
events.description: Sigismund III Vasa, king of Poland and grand duke of Lithuania since 1587, succeeded his father John III as King of Sweden. A zealous Catholic, he ruled Sweden until he was deposed in 1599.
events.html: Sigismund III Vasa, king of Poland and grand duke of Lithuania since 1587, succeeded his father John III as King of Sweden. A zealous Catholic, he ruled Sweden until he was deposed in 1599.

events.title: The Suez Canal opens
events.description: Empress Eugénie of France led a procession of ships through the new canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It cut thousands of kilometres from the sea route between Europe and Asia.
events.html: Empress Eugénie of France led a procession of ships through the new canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It cut thousands of kilometres from the sea route between Europe and Asia.

events.title: Luna 17 lands Lunokhod 1 on the Moon
events.description: The Soviet Luna 17 landed in the Sea of Rains and released Lunokhod 1, the first remote-controlled rover on another world. Driven from Earth, it travelled about 10 kilometres over ten months.
events.html: The Soviet Luna 17 landed in the Sea of Rains and released Lunokhod 1, the first remote-controlled rover on another world. Driven from Earth, it travelled about 10 kilometres over ten months.

events.title: Greek troops crush the Athens Polytechnic uprising
events.description: A tank broke through the gates of the Athens Polytechnic, ending a student occupation against the military junta. Dozens were killed, and the junta fell the following summer.
events.html: A tank broke through the gates of the Athens Polytechnic, ending a student occupation against the military junta. Dozens were killed, and the junta fell the following summer.

events.title: Police attack students in Prague, sparking the Velvet Revolution
events.description: Riot police beat students at a Prague march marking the anniversary of a Nazi crackdown. Outrage fuelled mass protests that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia within six weeks.
